key_insight: The paper shows that conventional FPV can decouple flamelet state from local strain, while an ε-based coupling keeps the flamelet response consistent with the modeled turbulence field.
engineering_relevance: For reacting-flow simulation, the ε-Z approach can improve physical consistency in high-strain regions and better represent quenching and product persistence in transonic mixing layers.
method: 2D RANS of a transonic accelerating reacting mixing layer
Compare one-step kinetics, conventional FPV, and proposed ε-Z flamelet model
Use ε to infer flamelet strain rate S* and transport selected species explicitly
evidence_signal: The abstract reports numerical comparison of the three models and shows that FPV tends to sample near-equilibrium states in high-strain regions, whereas ε-Z maintains a strain-consistent flamelet response.
watch_item: The ε-Z method adds model coupling and pressure/flameability-limit dependence, so robustness and calibration may be sensitive to the chosen turbulence closure and tabulated chemistry.
